Data independence and access

Unit 2 · Week 1 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the database foundations chapter, equipment-loans-flat.csv, database-foundations-workbook.md and database-foundations-answers.md. Use paper or a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL installation or student account is needed. Use the fixed reporting date of 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Data independence and access

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Introduce the equipment desk scenario. Explain which changes affect a report and who may change records. Activities are ungraded. Use only the supplied fictional loan records. Suggested timings are flexible. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

2. A report that stays the same

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual recall, then partner explanation

In this example, no. The report can still request LoanID and DueDate while the DBMS changes how it finds stored records. Introduce physical data independence as separation between storage details and application requests. Do not claim all changes preserve compatibility. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

3. Changes and report compatibility

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and discussion

An index illustrates physical data independence. Renaming a column changes the schema that the request uses. Moving systems may need conversion even when both are relational. A copied file does not guarantee compatibility with every DBMS. Use workbook question 10 to explain the limit. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

4. Access follows a requirement

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with student predictions

Discuss the minimum access needed for each role. A read-only availability report should not permit arbitrary edits or expose private borrower details. Product capabilities and configuration matter. SQLite relies on application and operating-system controls rather than server-style user accounts. Use the chapter’s stated scope. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

5. A check for each permission

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

These are proposed paper checks for the stated requirements, not a live system test. Partners explain what evidence would establish each result in an implemented system. Merely hiding an edit button is insufficient if another route still permits the edit. Never change live school records for this activity. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

6. Workbook practice and corrections

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use database-foundations-workbook.md and database-foundations-answers.md linked from the chapter. Q10: storage changes can preserve requests, schema changes may require edits. Q11: appropriately configured learner read access and staff update access. Q12: a small temporary list may suit CSV; reusable related facts and growing history favour relational management. Q13: counts depend on accurate return status and the fixed date/rule. No scores or assessment records are required. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

7. A changed overdue rule

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Choice and explanation

L002 now also qualifies. The original records stay the same and the rule changes from DueDate < reporting date to DueDate <= reporting date, with Returned=False still required. There are now three overdue loans: L001, L002 and L006. Four loans remain active. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

8. A final explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

An added index can change storage access without changing the report’s field request. Access restrictions need suitable controls and correct configuration, with checks against the requirements. Invite a fresh example: if Returned is renamed to ReturnStatus, a request naming Returned may need updating. Students record one idea to revisit. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.
